newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended down on Friday from the previous New York close on overseas sales as bearishness persisted and support from Asian physical buying was not forthcoming, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$365.00/50 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$365.25/75 close on Thursday.

Morning trade was quiet with little interest from Asian markets and physical buying remained light, but sales from funds and European players picked up during the afternoon session, bullion dealers said.
"I saw some selling from early Swiss players," said a bullion dealer at an international bank.
Support held well at $365 per ounce, traders said, but saw prices weakening further as bearishness persisted.
Gold would test lower, traders said, but estimates swung between $362 and $363 per ounce.
"The markets are still short, but funds and speculators expect selling from central banks and producers," another trader said.
Local gold ended HK$24 lower at HK$3,371 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -4.50 from its previous fix at -5.00.
